title: Castel Sant’Angelo began as Emperor Hadrian’s tomb; popes turned it into a fortress
body: Emperor Hadrian began his tomb by the Tiber in AD 135; his successor Antoninus Pius finished it in 139 and laid him there, and emperors were buried in it until Caracalla in 217. By the museum’s reconstruction it stood about 47.5 m high: a square base about 85 m wide and a round drum topped by an earth mound, with a ramp inside that turns one full circle up to the burial chamber. Its massive walls made a ready-made stronghold, and in the early 400s it was built into Rome’s city walls. Legend says the Archangel Michael appeared on top in 590, marking the end of a plague: hence the name, castle of the Holy Angel. In the 1390s the Roman entrance was sealed and a door 15 m up was reached by a drawbridge; in 1494–95 Pope Alexander VI added four bastions and a moat. The [Passetto](https://www.turismoroma.it/en/places/passetto-di-borgo), a walled corridor about 800 m long, links it to the Vatican, and in 1527 Pope Clement VII fled along it during the Sack of Rome. A museum since 1925, it still has Hadrian’s walls at its core, up to 44 m high.

slides.question: In which year did Pope Clement VII flee along a walled corridor from the Vatican to Castel Sant’Angelo?
slides.explanation: 1527, as the troops of Emperor Charles V sacked Rome. The corridor, the Passetto, is about 800 m long.

slides.alt: Animation in section on dark Tiber green: Hadrian's tomb rises, a square base, a round drum and an earth mound, with a spiral ramp to the burial chamber. City walls, the legendary angel and a chapel are added, the entrance is sealed, bastions and a moat appear, and the pope runs along the Passetto.

slides.prompt: Peel Castel Sant’Angelo back to Hadrian’s tomb: each time, tap the layer that was added last.
slides.takeaway: Each age built on and around the last: Alexander VI’s bastions, Nicholas V’s corner towers, the raised door, the chapel, the city walls, and at the core the tomb finished in AD 139.

slides.alt: Castel Sant’Angelo from across the Tiber: the massive round drum of Hadrian’s tomb, with brick storeys added on top and an angel statue above, behind crenellated outer walls and the river embankment.

events.text: It is built into Rome’s city walls.
Alexander VI adds bastions and a moat.

left.label: Hadrian’s tomb
left.text: A square base about 85 m wide and a round drum with an earth mound on top, about 47.5 m high, finished in AD 139.

right.label: Castel Sant’Angelo
right.text: The same Roman core, sealed and raised, inside four bastions, with papal rooms and an angel on top.

slides.question: Castel Sant’Angelo, the castle of the Holy Angel, takes its name from a legend about which figure?
slides.explanation: Legend says Michael appeared on top of Hadrian’s tomb in 590, sheathing his sword as a sign that a plague was over. A chapel to St Michael later crowned the castle.

source.label: Turismo Roma: Mausoleo di Adriano (Castel Sant’Angelo)
